items.evidence: Fixed in src/audio/index.ts (new `release` section, commit ec462fb76). Any source the engine stops (a bed, a voice, an ambience emitter, a jump's old source, a .m4a piece) now goes through retire(). Once its fade is due, it is disconnected along with its gain/filter/panner nodes and its buffer is set to null. Whichever comes first triggers this: onended; the wall clock reaching the stop while the context clock has also reached it; the context clock not moving between two looks; or, at once, a clock watch saying the clock is stalled. The watch runs every 250 ms: over at least 1 s, a context clock that moves less than 25% of wall time counts as stalled, and so does any state other than 'running'. While stalled, no one-shot starts and every pending fade and stale one-shot is freed. One-shots are also freed at their natural end by wall clock. stopBed and evictCues drop the evicted files from every cache: the buffers map, l.buf, the stream windows. Recovery: ctx.onstatechange and navigator.mediaDevices 'devicechange' look at the clock again (and resume a context the platform suspended or interrupted). When the clock comes back, only the bed the screen wants plays, and a retired bed has no buffer left to sound. A 'closed' context is dropped and rebuilt on the next gesture. Evidence: (1) node _harness/fw_r5_aud_release.mjs (report _harness/_reports/fw_r5_aud_release.json). Device sink, clock stuck at 0.01 s: menu 79 -> RIFT bed 137.6 -> menu 79 MB before AUD-4; after AUD-4, 45.2 -> 68.2 -> 45.2. The only live long sources left are the menu bed's (R1 and R2 PASS, load 42-364). Fake sink, same R1/R2. S1: the context is suspended mid-bed, the bed changed twice, then resumed, and exactly one bed plays: the draft (4 sources, 0 foreign), stalled=false. (2) probe_match_memory --track, run through _harness/fw_r5_aud_memrun.mjs (my own prod build at _harness/_prod/aud_r5). Device sink, audio at every Home is 45.2 MB: BRIDGE->RIFT gives home_0, bridge_home, rift_home = 45.2/45.2/45.2 (fw_r5_aud_mem_dev_br.json), and RIFT->BRIDGE->RIFT gives 45.2 x4 (fw_r5_aud_mem_dev_rbr.json). Round 4 had 385 / 674 / 922. Fake sink is the same, 45.2 at every Home (fw_r5_aud_mem_fake_br.json, fw_r5_aud_mem_fake_rbr.json). Load 108-553 throughout.

Long beds now stream (commits 7336977be, 813f1bbbe). A match bed's main stem and combat layer are kept compressed (2.3-2.7 MB each) and play by section windows (32 s + 0.3 s handles). The windows are decoded with WebCodecs AudioDecoder by the new src/audio/opus_stream.ts: an Ogg demux, packets placed by their TOC lengths, a 0.32 s pre-roll, and a frame count that must land exactly on the last packet's end. The next section is still chosen 3 s ahead from MUSIC_ACTS. A jump is the same equal-power 0.25 s fade over the same samples; a natural joint is a 30 ms linear fade over identical samples. The act's next window is decoded ahead. The menu and post-game loops stream too, one chain per stem of 16 s windows. The draft and the objective layer stay whole. Anything that cannot stream (.m4a/Safari, a context not at 48 kHz, no Opus AudioDecoder, a parse or decode failure) decodes whole as before. A window's buffers are reused once nothing holds them (2 pooled per stem), so a section change leaves no garbage. Evidence: node _harness/fw_r5_aud_stream.mjs (fw_r5_aud_stream.json): all 10 long stems (3 maps x main+intense at 32 s, menu x3 and postgame at 16 s) have the same length as decodeAudioData (7,680,000 / 3,072,000 / ...). Every window is bit-exact or has a peak error <= -113.8 dBFS. Decode takes 35-301 ms per window, load 14-127. probe_audio_music on the fake sink: 17/17 gates in fw_r5_aud_music2 and fw_r5_aud_music3 (with the pool). The bed holds 59.5 MB (objective 11.7 + windows 47.8) against 135 whole, at most 3 windows, 0 late. Clicks over the reference are -8.8 to -18.9 dB, peak -12.4 dBFS. The .m4a whole path is also 17/17 (fw_r5_aud_music_m4a.json). Measured, both sinks, probe_match_memory --track through fw_r5_aud_memrun: Home audio 79-80 -> 45.2 MB (fake) and 385-922 -> 45.2 (device). In-match audio: BRIDGE->RIFT 155.1/208.6->161.7 (device), 203.1->185.2/200.5-225.7->158.6 (fake, before the pool). RIFT->BRIDGE->RIFT 210.7->163.9 / 203.5->156.6 / 154.9 (device) and 209.6->168.7 / 154.4-182.4 / 171-174.9 (fake). Round 4 fake RIFT was 220-246. Match totals (not a valid ruling-20 reading at load 108-553): device RIFT 2570-2702, third RIFT 2690; fake third RIFT 2863 (round 4: 2953). items.evidence: Biggest cause found: the harness, not the client. Playwright sends Network.enable to every page with no buffer limits, so Chrome keeps a copy of every response body inside the renderer. The renderer's buffer partition at Home after one RIFT was 113.5 MB under Playwright (fw_r4_mem_r1_infra) and 7-28 MB without it (fw_r5_mem_infra_high). Renderer PartitionAlloc (footprint Tag 14) at Home after RIFT/BRIDGE/RIFT was 172/291/353 MB under Playwright (fw_r4_memv2_high_fake3) and 79/120/146 MB on the new raw-CDP driver (fw_r5_mem_raw_high3b). New tool _harness/fw_r5_mem_cdp.mjs drives the same Chrome with the same switches over CDP without the Network domain (probe --raw-cdp). A second source of false climb: dynamic resolution. One run drew RIFT's targets at 1536x864 and the next at 1920x1080, about 50 MB of GL textures apart. probe --full-scale turns it off so every match is read at its largest targets. Gate runs, all raw CDP, full-scale, fake sink, --track; load 90-597 so every verdict is NOT MEASURED (busy), memory numbers are raw readings. High RIFT/BRIDGE/RIFT: 2645/2719/2734 MB, climb +89 (fw_r5_mem_g2_ultra3.json; a High run despite the name, the preset flag did not split in zsh). Second High run: 2484/2625/2723, climb +239, FAIL (fw_r5_mem_g5_high3.json). Ultra RIFT/BRIDGE/RIFT: 2527/2628/2806, climb +279, FAIL (fw_r5_mem_g6_ultra3.json). Required order BRIDGE then RIFT: High 2584/2731 (fw_r5_mem_g6_high2.json), Ultra 2501/2768 (fw_r5_mem_g6_ultra2.json). Every match is under 3000 MB. Homes are 1183-1413 MB, all under 2500. The live set at every Home is +12 to +42 MB over first Home (gate is 150). Still open: the third RIFT's live objects match the first RIFT's within about 30 MB (GL textures 1117 vs 1121, audio, heap, backing), yet footprint is about 215 MB higher at the median. Of that, renderer Tag 14 goes from 136 to 266 MB in the match and the GPU process is +94 MB. GPU 'Owned physical footprint (unmapped)' at Home grows 69 -> 109 -> 131 MB. memory-infra shows renderer gpu/transfer and shared_memory going 25->60 and 30->67 MB in the second match. This is Chrome/ANGLE keeping memory after the page frees it; nothing the page holds explains it. The ruling 27 climb clause therefore fails 2 of 3 three-match runs (+239, +279).

GLB fetch/parse/decode now runs at most 4 at a time (Assets.gate), so each file lands, uploads and frees in turn instead of every file of the match decoding at once. After the change, first-20-s peak minus the steady max is -74 to -303 MB in 10 of 11 matches. The one exception is Ultra's third RIFT at +11 MB (its peak 2806 at 3 s, steady max 2795), still under the ~100 MB target. The probe now also reads the footprint through queue, draft and loading. Pre-HUD peaks are 1728-2528 MB, below each match's peak. Before the change, start transients were +107 to +140 MB (fw_r5_mem_smoke, fw_r5_mem_raw_ultra3).
